criteria.evidence: All five guided sections plus Agent intent are substantive, e.g. What it does: "It runs whenever a play is about to plan, break down or build from a node's ICE: the play calls the ready check (check_ice_workable.py) on that node, or on the whole model, before it starts."; Inputs/Outputs names flags and exit codes ("0 ready, 1 not ready, 2 the node is unknown or an input cannot be read"); eight Given/When/Then criteria; Out of scope names owners (fn-725, cap-718, /discover-domains).

Most rules carry their why ("A met intent counts because it was confirmed first and work that keeps it met is still wanted."; "A business intent page that is missing counts as not confirmed, so a link to an intent nobody wrote never makes a node ready."), but one does not: "A functionality with no capability yet (the holding folder) is warned about and is not ready." It states the what only, and does not say what the holding folder is or why such a functionality is both warned about and blocked rather than just one of the two.
criteria.fix: Rewrite that rule to say what the holding folder is and why: e.g. "A functionality with no capability yet (it sits in the holding folder, where functionalities wait until a capability claims them) is not ready, because readiness flows through a capability and it has none; the check also warns, so the Alignment loop picks it up to attach it."

criteria.evidence: Rules are discrete bullets ("A need that is not in the done list is open, and an open need makes the node blocked and not ready; the reason names what it waits for."); acceptance is Given/When/Then ("Given a capability with an empty domain that serves a confirmed business intent and needs nothing, when the ready check runs on it, then it is ready (exit 0) and its warnings include \"has no domain yet\"."); the function is stated as behavior, never as a user story.

Parent capability gives one line: "A capability or functionality is ready without a domain (fn-724) — the ready check drops the domain and reads confirmed intents and open needs instead." and the guiding rule "A capability is ready when it serves at least one confirmed (or met) business intent and nothing it needs is still open". The child adds inputs (`--done`, `--node`), exit codes, edge cases (missing intent page, domain id not in the spine, capability missing from the spine, no done list) and testable acceptance criteria.

What: "A capability is ready when it serves a confirmed business intent and nothing it needs is open; a functionality when its capability is ready and nothing it needs is open. A missing domain is a warning, never a block." Why: "That rule blocked a plan built straight from a business intent, which is what this functionality removes." Edges: "Checking that a need or identified-by link points at a real capability or functionality — ... (fn-725) owns that." and "Writing or fixing the domain link — /discover-domains adds it later". A cold reader can explain what, why and edges; the only undefined term is "the holding folder", covered under self_explanation.
